newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week December 27 - January 3.
**DECEMBER 27**
MOSCOW - An official says Sheremetyevo airport has completed the modernisation of its main runway.
* Sheremetyevo airport chief executive says cargo handling operations would be increased five percent this year compared with 1995. He did not give figures.
* Lufthansa Technik AG says it and Aeroflot have renewed an agreement under which the Germany group services the Russian international carrier's Airbus A-310-300 fleet.
**DECEMBER 30**
TAIPEI - Taiwan's aeronautics authority says it has reached initial agreement with U.S. firm FedEx under which the latter has agreed to set up an express cargo transhipment centre in Taiwan.
SINGAPORE - DHL says its Singapore operation recorded more than five million shipments for the first time in 1996, with electronics the main growth generator.

HONG KONG - Industry sources says illegal mobile phone use across the Chinese border is continuing to interrupt air traffic control communications with airline pilots flying in and out of Hong Kong but cross-border action to try and solve the problem appears to be working.
MIAMI - Experts says the phasing-out of some tax incentives for investment in Puerto Rico could drive business from the island and hurt and air cargo carriers that serve those businesses.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot domestic and CIS department deputy chief Leonid Mokhov says it will start regular passenger flights between Moscow and the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek from February.
BISHKEK - Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev decreed that the former Soviet Republic's national air carrier, Kyrgzstan Aba Zholduru, should be privatised.
PARIS - Air Liberte says the chairman of BA's French subsidiary TAT, Marc Rochet, was appointed chairman of the management board of Air Liberte.
**DECEMBER 31**
TAIPEI - The local Economic Daily News reported BA is likely to buy a stake of about 16 percent in Taiwan's China Airlines in a deal worth about T$6.3 billion.
LONDON - BA declines comment on a newspaper report from Taipei that it is set to buy a 16 percent stake in China Airlines.
HONG KONG - Cathay Pacific says its board has approved the appointment of Henry Fan, managing director of CITIC Pacific Ltd, as deputy chairman of the airline effective January 1.
PARIS - The Paris airports authority (ADP) says New York was the top originating gateway for import traffic into Charles de Gaulle and Orly airports last month, despite a strong decline in tonnage.
* ADP says New York was the top destination for imports and exports traffic from Charles de Gaulle and Orly airport in the first eleven months of 1996.
* The French transport ministry says ADP and Federal Express have formally signed an agreement covering the expansion of FedEx's main European hub at Charles de Gaulle airport.

SINGAPORE - Singapore Airlines's regional airline Silk Air says it has signed a sales and leaseback agreement with General Electric Capital Aviation Services for two of its four owned B737-300 aircraft.
ZURICH - American Airlines spokesman says it has decided to stop flying directly between Zurich and New York from February 1.
PARIS - Air France chief financial officer Patrice Durand says France is not yet in a position to adopt an open skies arrangement with the U.S..
TAMPA - Delta Air Lines Inc's Delta Express says it will begin three new daily, non-stop flights from January 1 between Tampa, Boston and add another flight from Boston to Orlando.
HONOLULU - Hawaiian Airlines, citing soft market conditions, says it was delaying the start of its new non-stop service between Seattle and Maui, Hawaii, until February 15 from January 18.
**JANUARY 1**
BEIJING - The Xinhua news agency says China's total freight traffic in Jan-Nov was 2.45 billion tonnes, down 0.1 percent from the same period last year.
NEW YORK - Kiwi International Air Lines says that it will detail its return to scheduled services on Jan 2.
**JANUARY 2**

BEIJING - The China Daily quoted Bao Peide, deputy director of the Civil Aviation Administration of China as saying "Despite frequent disasters in other parts of the world last year, China's aviation sector set a record of 29 months, and 2.33 million hours, of safe flying."
SYDNEY - BA Investments (Australia) Ltd says BA Plc's chief executive officer, Robert Ayling, has been appointed to the board of Qantas Airways Ltd.
PARIS - Figures issued by ADP show the Paris airports recorded the highest percentage gain in cargo traffic in November among the EU's top cargo-handling airports.
* ADP figures show Air France increases its share of global air cargo tonnage handled at the two Paris airport, Charles de Gaulle and Orly, in the first eleven months of 1996.
* Air France chairman Christian Blanc says he had become an ardent advocate of privatisation for the state-owned carrier and outlined plans for more cost cuts over the next three years.
* ADP figures show export traffic from the Paris airports totalled 53,722 tonnes, in November or up 8.4 percent on a year ago.
* ADP figures show November import traffic to the Paris airports, totalled 46,979 tonnes, an increase of ten percent on Nov 1995.
* ADP figures show air cargo exports from the Paris airports, totalled 537,880 tonnes in the first eleven months of 1996, down 0.9 percent on Jan-Nov 1995.
* ADP figures show Jan-Nov 1996 import traffic to the Paris, totalled 475,499 tonnes, an increase of 1.9 percent on a year ago.
GENEVA - Airport authority figures show Geneva's Cointrin airport handled 5,563 tonnes of air cargo in October 1996, a drop of 9.8 percent on Oct 1995.
PARIS - Airport authority figures show Rennes St-Jacques airport handled 3,025 tonnes of air cargo and trucked airfreight in the first ten months of 1996, an increase of 3.8 percent on 1995 levels.

AMSTERDAM - KLM Cargo's Cargovision magazine says KLM Cargo, Philips Electronics and Dutch and U.S. Customs are jointly developing a pilot database system to speed communications between them on Dutch-U.S. air shipments.
STOCKHOLM - Freight forwarders says several charterers flew to China from Sweden to handle a surge of air cargo volumes ahead of an increase in import fees into China which took effect on January 1.
BASLE - Airport authority figures show Jan-Nov cargo traffic handled at Basle-Mulhouse-Freiburg airport totalled 81,059 tonnes, an increase of 14 percent from a year ago.
PARIS - Air authority figures show Jan-Nov air cargo traffic at Strasbourg-Entzeim airport totalled 6,104 tonnes, up 8.8 percent on the previous year.
* Brest's Guipavas airport says it handled 3,044 tonnes of cargo traffic in Jan-Nov, an increase of 25 percent on the same period in 1995.
* Nice-Cote d'Azur airport reported a 16.5 percent increase in airfreight traffic for November over the same month in 1995.
* Air France figures show a 4.9 percent increase in cargo traffic for November 1996, with 428.4 million FTK's.
LONDON -UPS is introducing several new services in the U.S. and is raising some rates effective Feb 1.
NEW YORK - Kiwi International Air Lines says it will return to scheduled service January 20 with an emphasis on low fares, new marketing strategies and slow growth.
**JANUARY 3**
BEIJING - The Xinhua news agency says the Civil Aviation General Administration of China placed orders for 62 commercial planes with foreign aircraft manufacturers in 1996.
PARIS - An Emery Worldwide official says it has appointed Christian Ranchon sales manager for France.
* Pau-Pyrenees airport figures show Jan-Nov freight fell 0.2 percent to 1,096 tonnes from year ago figures. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
